FOLLOW THE LEADER

10 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available space

### EQUIPMENT

None needed. Can add 1 ball per player for dribbling loads

### DESCRIPTION

Players will work in groups of two (this can groups of three or four with higher numbers). The leader will move around the gym, attempting to be as creative in their movements as possible. They should explore a number of different movements, such as hopping, skipping, crawling, changing speed, etc. The players in a line behind the leader must attempt to keep up and shadow their movements as closely as possible. Change the leader every 30 to 45 seconds.

### SCORING

N/A

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Changing movement, direction and speed

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- The leader can freeze like a statue at any time. They attempt to trick the players in their group by getting them to freeze too late.
- Players must always remain on the floor.
- Add a ball for dribbling.

### STAFF ROLE

- Encourage creativity in movement.
- Encourage players to use the whole space in a random manner.

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- Try not to repeat the same movement twice
- What other ways could you move?

ROCK, PAPER, SCISSORS TAG

10 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available space (no baskets needed)

### EQUIPMENT

None needed. Can add 1 ball per player for dribbling loads.

### DESCRIPTION

Players partner up and play a game of rock-paper-scissors. Whoever wins the game has to try and tag their partner. The loser attempts to escape, attempting to stay alive without being tagged for seven seconds. Change partners every two repetitions.

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Play with your feet instead of hands. Players hop and then reveal their stance on the 3 count.
- Feet together = rock, feet apart = paper, feet staggered = scissors.
- Add a ball for dribbling.
- Play 1-on-1 where the winner attempts to score the lay-up while the loser tries to defend while holding their ball.

### SCORING

N/A

### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure players count the seven seconds to stay alive.
- Constrain the space if too difficult (e.g. play the tag in a smaller area).
- Make sure players know their 1-on-1 baskets to play on.

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Changing movement, direction and speed
- Exploring creative finishing

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- How else could you have finished that lay-up?
- What would you do differently on the next repetition?
- Are you remembering to change partners frequently?

GAME TIME

is where players participate in different activities and games designed to stimulate their growth and development.

These activities have been carefully created to mimic the game of basketball. With the NBA Basketball School Camp Curriculum, players develop technically and tactically through the actual act of playing basketball itself.

Each Game Time activity is clearly described and presented in the following format: name, time, space, equipment, description, scoring, types of loads, staff roles, key concepts, and guiding questions. Coaches are encouraged to utilize the information presented and to expand on those ideas in a way that would be most meaningful to their players.

MODULE 6: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

### I-ON-2 TOUCHDOWN

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available space (no baskets needed). Mark out a rectangle using 6 cones with every cone approximately 6 steps away.

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per player, 6 cones per group

#### DESCRIPTION

An offensive player with a ball will begin at the start position, with one defender positioned in the first half of the rectangle and a second defender in the second half. The offense has 10 seconds to dribble to the end zone and score a touchdown. Each defender is limited to their areas and must try to prevent the offensive player from scoring a touchdown. The defenders must also dribble a ball while they defend. Players must rotate one spot up after each repetition is finished (e.g. offense will become the last defender in the second half of the rectangle, the second defender will move up to the first half, etc.).

#### SCORING

Offensive players will receive 1 point for successfully scoring a touchdown.

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Identifying the open space
- Manipulating the ball in tight spaces
- Beating first and second line of defense

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Defenders can only use one hand to defend.
- The statue load: defensive players are not allowed to move their feet once the offensive player starts dribbling.
- The crab load: defensive players are only allowed to move laterally side to side.
- The offense has seven dribbles to get to the other end of the rectangle (for younger players, allow 4 more dribbles to be taken). Retreat dribbles do not deduct from dribble limit. The last defender must call out the total number of dribbles.
- The defense can hold their balls and can reach for the offense ball to try and steal it.
- The defense is completely live.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Create the rectangles as quickly as possible.
- Remind the last defender to count down from 10 seconds in their leadership voice.
- Watch to check that the defenders stay in their respective areas within the rectangle
- Help players identify and use open space

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- Where is the space?
- How could you trick the defenders?

### I-ON-I+I CLOSEOUT SERIES

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

#### DESCRIPTION

In groups of three, the shooter will start in any location in the mid-range or behind the 3PT line. The passer will stand in any location within a reasonable passing distance to the shooter, with the defender in a random location between two to four meters away from the shooter (approximately four to eight big steps). As soon as the ball leaves the passer hands, the defender can begin to closeout. The offense has two dribbles to score. After three quick repetitions from different locations, the players will change roles.

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- The defender can only use one hand to contest.
- The passer must dribble and send a one handed pass to the defender.
- The repetition is only over when the defense rebounds the ball. The offense can therefore keep going if they secure the offensive rebound.
- The shooter can pass back to the passer and get open again if they get stuck or the defense recovers to neutral.

#### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure players change locations after every repetition.
- Ensure the defense stands four to eight steps away and closes out from different positions.
- Officiate the maximum two dribble load.

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Closing out on defense by running out quick and stopping naturally (no choppy steps)
- Attacking closeouts without traveling

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- What other location or angle have you not played from yet?
- Can you explore different ways to pass?
